rows.title: U.S. Considers $100,000 Fee For Foreign Students Seeking Post-Graduation Work
rows.body: The United States is considering charging foreign students $100,000 if they want to work after graduation. According to ChainCatcher, the proposal was reported by Jin10 and does not include additional details.

rows.title: Dragonfly Partner Haseeb Says Crypto Industry Helped Lay Groundwork for AI Boom
rows.body:
Dragonfly partner Haseeb said on X that the current AI boom might have been harder to emerge without the development of the crypto industry. According to Odaily, he said Bitcoin miners’ experience over the past decade in power access, site selection, and large-scale infrastructure in remote areas helped form a foundation for today’s AI data center expansion.

He also said crypto mining demand helped Nvidia shift from a gaming GPU maker to a supplier of AI computing chips. Haseeb added that the core teams at several emerging AI cloud providers, including CoreWeave, Crusoe, Together AI, and Nscale, also have backgrounds in the crypto industry.

rows.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Say Six Vessels Tried to Pass Under U.S. Air Cover
rows.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said six vessels tried to pass under U.S. warplane escort, and after two had accidents, the other vessels quickly turned back. According to Jin10, the shipping company owner should ask the crews of those six ships whether the strait is clear, rather than asking the U.S. Central Command.

rows.title: STOCKS | Blackstone to Buy HSBC Australia's $25 Billion Home Loan Book
rows.body:
Blackstone Inc. has agreed to acquire an about A$36 billion, or $25 billion, Australian home loan portfolio from HSBC Holdings Plc, people familiar with the matter said, according to Bloomberg.

The deal is set to be one of the largest home loan portfolio transactions ever.

rows.title: Israeli Forces Bomb Southern Lebanon's Taybeh
rows.body: Israeli forces bombed Taybeh in southern Lebanon, according to JIN10. According to ChainCatcher, the report did not provide further details on casualties or damage.

rows.title: Shiba Inu Price Prediction Hinges On $0.00000446 Support
rows.body:
Shiba Inu (SHIB) rose 28% last week before sellers capped the rally at $0.00000548, leaving August 2026 trading focused on $0.00000446 support. The token also has delayed Shibarium upgrades, including a privacy rollout with Zama, as catalysts, according to BeInCrypto, alongside progress on Shiba Eternity, the SHIB Metaverse relaunch and a LEASH v2 roadmap.

Weekly momentum has improved for the first time since March 2024, but SHIB remains in a broader 2026 downtrend. The token traded at $0.00000461, with sellers defending $0.00000548 and support below at $0.00000405.

rows.title: Universal Music Subscription Revenue Tops Estimates on Price Hikes
rows.body:
Universal Music Group NV said second-quarter subscription revenue beat analysts’ expectations as streaming platforms raised prices and the company benefited from a busy release schedule, according to Bloomberg.

The result suggests higher subscription fees are helping offset broader pressures in the music business.

rows.title: AI TRENDS | Benchmark Partner Chetan Puttagunta Questions Anthropic's Call for Tighter Model Distillation Rules
rows.body:
Benchmark partner Chetan Puttagunta said on X that Anthropic's public call for tighter regulation of AI model distillation was confusing. According to PANews, he said Anthropic is currently valued at about $1 trillion and has significant technical and financial resources, and that large-scale distillation attacks should, in theory, be easier to identify and track at that scale.

Puttagunta added that if Anthropic chooses to restrict such activity, the real cost may not be a lack of technical capability but giving up some API revenue. He said the only cost that appears to be required is reduced income from related API business. Anthropic and other AI companies have previously continued to focus on model distillation issues.

rows.title: Hyperliquid HIP-3 Open Interest Reaches Record $3.92 Billion
rows.body: HyperliquidNews posted on X that HIP-3 open interest reached $3.92 billion, a record high. According to Odaily, the figure marks an all-time high for the protocol.

rows.title: South Korea Completes Draft of Digital Asset Framework Bill
rows.body:
South Korea’s Financial Services Commission said it has completed a draft of the Digital Asset Framework Bill and is working to coordinate the remaining issues before legislation moves forward. According to ChainCatcher, the National Assembly’s agenda for the second half of the year has been set, and lawmakers plan to accelerate the bill’s progress where possible.

South Korea is also considering adding a legal basis for AI agent payments to the bill. The proposed framework would authorize rules for customer identification, payment liability allocation, foreign exchange reporting for cross-border transactions, and programmable payment standards, as officials prepare for a future in which AI could become a major participant in small, high-frequency payments.

rows.title: Amazon Set To Report Second-Quarter Earnings As Investors Watch Capex, AWS
rows.body: According to CNBC, Amazon is set to report second-quarter earnings after the bell on Thursday, with analysts surveyed by LSEG expecting earnings per share of $1.82 on revenue of $196.47 billion. Wall Street is also looking for Amazon Web Services revenue of $40.54 billion and advertising revenue of $19.43 billion, while investors focus on capital spending after Amazon’s first-quarter capex reached $44.2 billion, up 77% from a year earlier, and is expected to rise to $49.3 billion in the second quarter. Amazon kept its February guidance for roughly $200 billion in capex in 2026, though some analysts now expect the company to lift that forecast. Morgan Stanley analysts said earlier this month that Amazon’s capex could reach $218 billion this year and rise to $318 billion in 2028, while they also pointed to cloud deals and partnerships with OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta. AWS revenue is expected to increase about 31% from a year ago, compared with 28% growth in the first quarter, which was its fastest expansion in more than three years. Amazon also held layoffs in its customer service and seller support divisions in recent months and announced job cuts in its artificial general intelligence unit last week. The company brought Prime Day forward from its usual July schedule during the second quarter, and Adobe said U.S. online spending across all retailers during the June 23 through June 26 event rose 9.3% year over year to $26.4 billion.

rows.title: 71% of S&P 500 Stocks Trade Above 200-Day Average as PayPal, GoDaddy, DoorDash Rise
rows.body:
According to CNBC, about 71% of S&P 500 stocks have climbed above their 200-day moving averages, the highest level in two years, even as the broader index has not set a new high since June 2. The article said the move suggests investors are putting money into stocks outside the artificial intelligence trade, including megacaps and chipmakers.

Among the names highlighted, PayPal recently moved above its 200-day moving average after reporting second-quarter results that topped analyst estimates. The payments company said payment volume reached $486.4 billion and raised its full-year earnings guidance. CNBC's David Faber also confirmed that Stripe and Advent International made a joint $53.4 billion offer to buy PayPal. GoDaddy also moved above its 200-day average after reaffirming a full-year free cash flow target of about $1.8 billion in its first-quarter report. DoorDash eclipsed its 200-day average and said it secured FAA certification for commercial drone deliveries, while Cintas is approaching a golden cross, when the 50-day moving average rises above the 200-day moving average.

rows.title: Ondo Finance Weighs Acquisition Worth Up To $500 Million
rows.body: Ondo Finance is evaluating a potential acquisition valued at $250 million to $500 million as consolidation accelerates across crypto infrastructure. According to CoinDesk, the tokenized-assets firm has not appointed formal advisers and is considering wealthtech targets, among other subsectors, while an Ondo representative said it is not in conversations with any party at this time.

rows.title: FIFA's Infantino Seeks More Revenue After Record World Cup
rows.body:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino has announced a plan for football's governing body to generate even more money after a World Cup that set records for attendance, ticket prices and revenue, according to Bloomberg.

UEFA and fans oppose the funding plan.

rows.title: RedStone: Tokenized Gold Surges, But DeFi Collateral Use Remains Low
rows.body:
Demand for tokenized gold has surged this year as physical bullion climbed to record highs, but only a small share of the asset is being used in decentralized finance, according to a new report by RedStone. According to Cointelegraph, tokenized gold spot trading volume reached $90.7 billion in the first quarter as gold futures rallied above $5,600 per troy ounce. RedStone said only about $63 million worth of Tether Gold (XAUT) and PAX Gold (PAXG) is currently being used as collateral on Aave v3 and Morpho, equal to just 1.5% of the tokens’ combined $4.2 billion market capitalization. The report said this points to a major adoption gap even as tokenized bullion gains attention in broader markets.

RedStone also said tokenized gold has already gone through a meaningful stress test. On March 23, Aave processed its largest cluster of XAUT liquidations without disruption during a sharp sell-off in gold, showing that tokenized bullion can operate reliably as DeFi collateral under market pressure. The liquidation event came after gold fell 10% over the previous week, marking its worst weekly performance in more than four decades. JPMorgan precious metals strategist Greg Shearer described the sell-off as an “extremely brutal flush.” Since peaking in January, gold futures have declined more than 26%, pressured by expectations of higher US interest rates, which reduced demand for non-yielding assets such as precious metals. RedStone said the limited use of tokenized gold in lending protocols highlights an infrastructure challenge as tokenized real-world assets continue to scale. Gold is part of a broader tokenized RWA market that also includes private credit and US Treasurys, with equities growing in importance. In June, Token Terminal reported that the sector had topped $43 billion in value. Meanwhile, centralized crypto exchanges are increasingly embracing tokenized assets as they try to connect traditional finance and digital assets. According to a recent CoinGecko report, the emerging “crypto TradFi” market had grown to $6.6 billion as of June.

rows.title: STOCKS | Nasdaq 100 Gains 3% as AI Trade Rebounds
rows.body:
The Nasdaq 100 gained 3% as giant chipmakers rallied and dip buyers returned on speculation that the artificial-intelligence trade has more room to run, according to Bloomberg.

The rebound lifted stocks after a rout in the group that has helped power the bull market.

rows.title: Crypto for Advisors: Is the Clarity Act Dead?
rows.body:
The pending Digital Asset Market Clarity Act may be dead after Senate Majority Leader John Thune said the bill will not pass before September, with critics also attacking its “ethics” language on federal officials issuing crypto tokens. The debate centers on whether the bill can establish clearer asset classification and disclosure rules, according to CoinDesk, while avoiding subjective definitions and conflicting SEC-CFTC standards.

Experts quoted in the newsletter said the measure could still help investors by separating fundraising transactions from underlying tokens, but warned that implementation and enforcement would determine whether it reduces uncertainty or just shifts it into rulemaking.

rows.title: Apple's Gross Margin Guidance In Focus Ahead of Thursday Earnings
rows.body: According to CNBC, Apple will report fiscal 2026 third-quarter earnings after the bell on Thursday, and investors are watching for management's forward guidance on how the company is handling a memory-chip shortage and rising input costs. The article says gross margin will be a key metric, with Apple having guided third-quarter gross margin to 47.5% to 48.5% in April, while analysts at Jefferies expect the profit margin on each iPhone 17 to fall by 4 to 9 percentage points and see gross margin still contracting by 3.5 percentage points even if Apple raises prices 18% to 26% on higher-end iPhone 18 models. Apple stock was trading near record highs, and the company recently became the second U.S. company to top a $5 trillion market cap, following Nvidia.

rows.title: Jordi Visser Says AI’s Easy Money Is Over, Bitcoin Is Next
rows.body:
Veteran macro investor Jordi Visser said the easy money in artificial intelligence is over and that Bitcoin is where the next big gains may emerge. The view comes as Big Tech’s AI spending is pressuring free cash flow, with Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet all seeing cushions shrink, according to BeInCrypto, while Google parent Alphabet posted negative free cash flow last quarter for the first time since its 2004 listing.

Visser said he still sees AI returns, but at a much lower rate, and pointed to blockchain rails for autonomous AI payments. He also expects Ethereum to benefit more than Bitcoin because investors are favoring fee-generating networks.

rows.title: European Stocks Close Mostly Higher on July 30
rows.body: European major stock indexes closed mostly higher on July 30, with the UK FTSE 100 down 0.10%, France's CAC 40 up 0.93%, Germany's DAX 30 up 0.45%, and Italy's FTSE MIB up 1.29%, according to Jiemian News.

rows.title: Citi: Warsh’s Broader Inflation Focus Could Lower Chances of Near-Term Rate Hikes
rows.body: According to Jin10, Citi economists Andrew Hollenhorst and Veronica Clark said Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signaled that inflation measures other than the personal consumption expenditures price index, or PCE, would play a larger role in monetary policy, which lowered the likelihood of a near-term Fed rate hike. They said core PCE inflation fell from 3.4% in June to 3.3%, while core consumer price index inflation was 2.6%, closer to the Federal Reserve's 2% inflation target. Hollenhorst and Clark also said markets should increasingly see over the next few months that the broader inflation measures Warsh is watching do not show worrying signs of accelerating inflation. Markets currently price a 59% chance of a Fed rate hike in September, but the two economists said that expectation may be wrong.

rows.title: Trump Says He Could Withdraw Todd Blanche Nomination Temporarily
rows.body: According to Axios, President Trump said Thursday he would have "no objection" to temporarily withdrawing acting Attorney General Todd Blanche's nomination until his Republican opponents are out of office next January. Trump directed the comment at GOP Sens. Thom Tillis of North Carolina and John Cornyn of Texas, saying the move would come after their concerns stalled Blanche's nomination. Trump also called Blanche "a STAR" and said he would "remain, in any event, as Acting."

rows.title: Microsoft's Goldilocks AI Quarter
rows.body: Microsoft's blockbuster earnings sparked a major rally as TD Cowen's Derrick Wood told Bloomberg TV the company delivered a "Goldilocks" quarter, with accelerating Azure growth, improving AI economics and surging Copilot adoption. Bloomberg reported Wall Street sees Microsoft's AI story strengthening further.

rows.title: Man Yue Technology Starts Production On 20Ah LCC Line
rows.body:
Man Yue Technology (0894) said its self-developed lithium carbon capacitor, or LCC, has begun production on a new 20Ah single-cell line at the end of June, according to Ming Pao.

The company said the line is the world's first large-capacity, fully automated intelligent production line, with annual output reaching 1.5GWh based on 10C charge and discharge. It said the line gives it the world's highest annual production capacity in the supercapacitor sector and marks the start of mass production for its self-developed LCC technology, laying the groundwork for large-scale market supply.

rows.title: STOCKS | Kingboard Group, Kingboard Laminate Issue Profit Warnings
rows.body:
Kingboard Group (0148) and Kingboard Laminate (1888) both issued profit alerts after recent sharp share-price declines, saying first-half earnings rose on stronger pricing and sales, according to Ming Pao.

The two companies said copper-clad laminate panels and upstream raw materials remained in short supply, which pushed up product selling prices and volumes. Kingboard Laminate said its first-half net profit is expected to jump by more than twofold year on year to above HK$2.8 billion.

rows.title: STOCKS | Jardine Matheson H1 Base Profit Rises 9%
rows.body:
Jardine Matheson Holdings (SGX: J36) said its base profit for the six months ended June rose 9% year on year to $735 million, or HK$5.733 billion, according to Ming Pao.

Reported profit attributable to shareholders increased 3% to $542 million, while interim dividend per share rose 8% to $0.65.

The group left its full-year earnings guidance unchanged, but raised its full-year dividend guidance to at least $2.47 per share.

rows.title: Qualcomm CEO: Memory Chip Prices Are Rising Sharply
rows.body: According to Jin10, Qualcomm CEO said memory chip prices are rising very sharply, and higher prices are changing consumer behavior.

rows.title: MIDDAY MOVES | AI Infrastructure Stocks Retreat on Debt Concerns; Manhattan Associates Soars 25%, Lemonade Sinks 22%
rows.body: According to CNBC, artificial intelligence cloud computing stocks retreated Wednesday amid concerns over the debt AI companies have amassed and a backlash against data centers, with Nebius down more than 8%, Lumentum off 7% and CoreWeave tumbling more than 7% to a 52-week intraday low, pressured in part by insider stock sales. Manhattan Associates soared 25% after second-quarter earnings and revenue topped estimates and the supply chain software provider raised its full-year profit and revenue forecasts. Lemonade tanked 22% after the insurance company said gross spending rose 30% to $64 million in the second quarter while technology development expense grew 34% to $30 million. Lennox International plummeted 20% after the heating and air conditioning maker trimmed full-year earnings guidance to a range of $23 to $24 per share, down from $23.50 to $25; the FactSet consensus was $24.44. Vertiv tumbled 16% on mixed second-quarter results, as organic revenue grew 17.8%, below the FactSet consensus of 23.6%, even though earnings and revenue beat estimates. SoFi Technologies dropped 9% to a 52-week low despite a top- and bottom-line beat, raised full-year revenue guidance and reaffirmed EPS guidance, as technology platform revenue declined. KLA Corp slid 9% after issuing disappointing guidance, seeing first-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.16 per share, plus or minus 10 cents, versus the LSEG estimate of $1.14. Caterpillar fell more than 7% after Baird Equity Research downgraded the stock to neutral, with the analyst noting growing momentum behind data center opposition. NXP Semiconductors lost 7% and PPG Industries fell 6%. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) tumbled nearly 4% for a fifth straight day, with Advanced Micro Devices down 5%, Nvidia off nearly 3% and Broadcom down almost 2%. Procter & Gamble dropped over 2% after fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $21.2 billion missed the LSEG forecast of $21.38 billion. On the upside, GE HealthCare Technologies rose 10% after posting adjusted EPS of $1.13, beating a FactSet consensus of $1.04, and reaffirming full-year guidance. Rocky Brands surged about 15% as adjusted EPS more than tripled from a year earlier, aided by tariff refunds. Mondelez jumped 4% after posting second-quarter profit of 73 cents a share on revenue of $9.36 billion, topping LSEG estimates of 68 cents and $9.20 billion. Ford Motor climbed 3% on an earnings beat and raised its 2026 outlook, though automotive revenue slightly missed. Teradyne gained 3% and Biogen rose 2% after beating estimates and raising full-year adjusted EPS guidance, while Skyworks Solutions slumped 3%.

rows.title: Magnum Sales Growth Beat Fails to Impress Investors
rows.body:
Magnum Ice Cream Co. posted quarterly organic sales growth that beat expectations, but the maker of Cornetto and Ben & Jerry’s did not raise its outlook, disappointing investors, according to Bloomberg reported.

The company’s cautious guidance overshadowed the stronger sales performance.

rows.title: GEOPOLITICS | UEFA Threatens World Cup Boycott Over FIFA Stake Sale
rows.body:
UEFA’s 55 member nations have resolved to boycott FIFA tournaments if President Gianni Infantino proceeds with plans to sell World Cup stakes to private investors, according to Bloomberg.

The decision adds pressure on FIFA as Infantino pursues the proposed sale to private investors.

rows.title: Disney Seeks FCC End to ABC Station License Probe
rows.body: Walt Disney Co. asked the Federal Communications Commission to drop its probe into the licenses of its eight ABC TV stations, according to Bloomberg. More than 150,000 public comments have been submitted, mostly supporting Disney's effort to keep the licenses.

rows.title: STOCKS | Equinix Seeks at Least $3 Billion From Data Center Debt Sale
rows.body: Equinix Inc. is seeking to raise at least $3 billion through a sale of U.S. investment-grade bonds, according to Bloomberg. The data center company is selling into a recently weakened market for debt tied to the artificial intelligence boom.

rows.title: BOE's Bailey Cites 'Huge Uncertainty' After Rates Held at 3.75%
rows.body:
Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said there is "huge uncertainty" in the world, including around energy prices, after the Monetary Policy Committee held interest rates at 3.75% in July, according to Bloomberg.

Bailey also said he thinks the labor market is showing softness.

rows.title: AI | Bargain Airfares Face Threat From AI Pricing
rows.body:
Airlines are adopting AI tools to squeeze more revenue from each flight, potentially reducing the chance of finding cheap seats on popular routes, according to Bloomberg.

The piece says bargain airfares may become harder to find as carriers use pricing technology to maximize revenue.

rows.title: U.S. 4-Week Treasury Auction Stop-Out Rate Falls to 3.63%
rows.body: According to Jin10, the U.S. Treasury auction stop-out rate for 4-week bills through July 30 was 3.63%, versus 3.73% previously.

rows.title: U.S. Central Command Rebuts Three Latest IRGC Claims
rows.body: U.S. Central Command said Iran's state media has continued spreading false information released by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps over the past few hours. According to Jin10, it rejected the IRGC's claim that the free and open shipping lane in the Strait of Hormuz is dangerous for commercial vessels, said recent Iranian attacks on U.S. forces did not destroy or damage any U.S. aircraft, and denied that the commercial oil tanker M/T Nora had broken through the U.S. blockade.

rows.title: U.S. 8-Week Treasury Auction Results: Yield and Allocation Rate
rows.body: According to Jin10, the U.S. 8-week Treasury auction on July 30 showed a stop-out yield and an allocation percentage of 19.59%, compared with 87.33% previously.

rows.title: Middle East Oil Ship-to-Ship Transfers Rebound After Brief Slowdown
rows.body:
Ship-to-ship crude transfer services in the Strait of Hormuz have become active again after a recent slowdown, helping move millions of barrels out of the strait. According to Jin10, the transport method has regained a key role as hostility in the Middle East escalates.

The transfer model emerged during the most intense period of conflict and became an important lifeline for some oil producers to maintain exports. Vessels typically move crude out of the Persian Gulf with their AIS transponders turned off to avoid detection, then carry out ship-to-ship transfers with another tanker outside the Strait of Hormuz before the second vessel delivers the crude to buyers around the world. Although the volume of crude moving through the strait remains below prewar levels, the barrels that have been shipped have helped ease market concern over a surge in oil prices. At least two shipping companies involved in the Strait of Hormuz trade are now handling volumes close to levels seen before the escalation, according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter.

rows.title: Situational Awareness Sells Large Portion of $16 Billion Public Equity Holdings to Citadel
rows.body: According to the Financial Times, hedge fund Situational Awareness, founded and run by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner and managing $24 billion, has quickly sold a large portion of its $16 billion public equity holdings to Citadel because of huge losses.

rows.title: U.S. 4-Week Treasury Auction Allocation Rate Rises to 50.42%
rows.body: According to Jin10, the U.S. 4-week Treasury auction allocation rate was 50.42%, compared with 11.81% previously.

rows.title: BOE’s Bailey Says Britain’s Static Labor Market Is Driving Youth Unemployment
rows.body:
Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said Britain’s static labor market is behind the surge in youth unemployment, according to Bloomberg.

Bailey said the low-hire, low-fire economy is hitting young workers the hardest.

rows.title: Citadel Buys Most Of AI Hedge Fund Situational Awareness's Stock Portfolio
rows.body: Citadel, the investment firm led by Ken Griffin, has acquired most of the stock portfolio held by AI hedge fund Situational Awareness, according to The Wall Street Journal. According to ChainCatcher, the move comes after the fund, founded by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, was forced to sell stock assets to ease liquidity pressure following large losses on AI-related trades. CNBC previously reported that the fund had fully exited all public-market equity positions.

rows.title: Citadel Acquires Most of AI Hedge Fund Situational Awareness’s Stock Portfolio
rows.body:
Citadel, the investment firm founded by Ken Griffin, has acquired most of the stock portfolio held by AI hedge fund Situational Awareness, according to people familiar with the matter. According to Odaily, Situational Awareness was forced to sell stock assets to ease liquidity pressure after suffering heavy losses from AI-related trades.

The fund was founded by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner. CNBC reported that the fund has liquidated all of its public-market stock positions.

rows.title: AI TRENDS | Jim Cramer Says Situational Awareness Liquidation May Signal AI Market Clearing Event
rows.body:
CNBC host Jim Cramer said the liquidation of all public stock positions by Situational Awareness, the fund behind the so-called “AI stock god,” may mean the AI sector is entering a market clearing event. According to Odaily, Cramer said markets are often near a short-term bottom after leveraged money and forced selling have been fully released.

He also said that going long AI hardware and shorting software is not a strategy used by a single fund, and that the liquidation could have a broader effect on the AI trade.

rows.title: Eversource Energy Rises 11.2% In 3 Months Ahead Of Q2 Earnings
rows.body:
According to CNBC, Eversource Energy is set to report second-quarter earnings today after the close, with a conference call scheduled for tomorrow morning at 9 a.m., as investors watch for any update to full-year guidance after the regulated utility raised its annual dividend 5% to $3.15 and cut 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $4.57 to $4.72 from $4.80 to $4.95. The company said the revision followed a cut in the base return on equity for New England transmission owners from 10.57% to 9.57% earlier this year, which it said would trim about $70 million in annual after-tax profit.

Eversource, which serves about 4.6 million customers across Connecticut, Massachusetts and New Hampshire, posted 11.2% gains over the past three months and 20.9% over the past year. The stock cleared $71 on June 24 after trading between roughly $66 and $72 during the spring and early summer, and it hit $75 this week after twice failing at that level over the past year.

rows.title: Whale Accumulates 1,050 WBTC and 66,300 ETH Over the Past Month
rows.body: A whale has continued adding WBTC and ETH over the past month, buying 1,050 WBTC at an average price of $64,277 and 66,300 ETH at an average price of $1,758. According to Odaily, the holdings are currently in profit by $10.8 million.

rows.title: Aave Founder Welcomes Justin D'Errico as Zapper Engineering Team Joins
rows.body:
Aave founder Stani Kulechov said on X that Justin D'Errico has joined the team and that the full Zapper engineering team has been hired. According to Foresight News, Kulechov said users who liked Zapper would like Aave Pro.

Justin D'Errico previously announced that he had joined Aave as chief backend engineer and would help the team become data-first and support future scaling. According to Foresight News, DeFi asset management platform Zapper said it will shut down on August 3.

rows.title: Polymarket LoL Submarket Jumps to 90% on Baron Kill Outcome
rows.body: A Polymarket submarket tied to the LCK Legends Group match between Hanwha Life Esports and Dplus KIA saw the "yes" option on "both sides kill Baron" surge from 50% one hour earlier to 90%, a 40-point jump. According to ChainCatcher, the move reflects a sharp swing in the prediction market tied to the event.

rows.title: Standard Chartered, Deutsche Bank Launch New Buybacks as Chinese Banks Stay on the Sidelines
rows.body:
Standard Chartered and Deutsche Bank both said in recent results that they will begin a new round of share repurchases. Standard Chartered announced on July 29 with its first-half 2026 results that it will pay an interim ordinary dividend of $0.204 per share, up 66%, and immediately start an additional $1 billion buyback after already completing $1.5 billion of repurchases in the first half, according to Jiemian News.

On the same day, Deutsche Bank said in its second-quarter results that it plans to launch a new €500 million share buyback in the second half after finishing its current €1 billion repurchase program. Chief financial officer Raja Akram said the bank's CET1 ratio stood at 13.9% and that strong internal capital generation gives it room to grow the business and deliver returns to shareholders.

Chinese banking analysts cited by Jiemian News said buybacks can reduce share capital, lift earnings per share and return on equity, and help support valuation when capital adequacy is comfortably above regulatory requirements. They also said Chinese banks have not yet launched buyback plans, citing capital constraints, regulatory approval hurdles, and the fact that repurchased shares generally must be cancelled and capital reduced rather than held as treasury stock. News of the banks' buyback plans comes as Chinese listed lenders continue to face questions about whether share repurchases could be used for market-value management and shareholder returns.

rows.title: Jim Cramer Says Forced AI Hedge Fund Selling May Help Stabilize Trade
rows.body:
According to CNBC, Jim Cramer said Thursday that forced selling tied to leveraged hedge-fund bets on artificial intelligence stocks may help steady the volatile AI trade. He made the comments on "Squawk on the Street" after David Faber reported that prime brokers for Situational Awareness, the AI-focused hedge fund founded by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, were trying to find buyers for some of the fund's holdings. Faber later said the fund's entire book of public investments had been sold after steep losses in recent weeks on its AI positions.

Situational Awareness has been bullish on AI infrastructure names such as Micron and CoreWeave while betting against software companies seen as vulnerable to AI disruption. Aschenbrenner's fund had amplified those bets with borrowed money, which can increase gains when trades work but can also magnify losses and force selling when they do not. Cramer said the liquidation could mark a bottom because many investors are using margin in the same stocks.
